people.solomon.meaning: He asks God for wisdom at Gibeon. He builds the temple with help from Huram of Tyre. He prays at its dedication, and fire comes down from heaven. Hezekiah’s Passover joy is the greatest in Jerusalem since his time.
people.david.role: Earlier king whose plans and promise guide later kings
people.david.meaning: Solomon is already king in his place when the book opens. Solomon builds the temple on the site David chose. Later kings follow his orders for priests, Levites, and music. God keeps David’s house because of the covenant with him.
people.moses.role: Earlier leader whose law guides temple worship
people.moses.meaning: He made the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness. He put the two tablets in the ark at Horeb. Later kings and priests follow his law for offerings, a tax, and Passover.
people.bezalel.role: Maker of the bronze altar at Gibeon
people.bezalel.meaning: He made the bronze altar that stands at Gibeon. Solomon offers one thousand burnt offerings on it. The book names him only here.
people.hiram.role: King of Tyre who sends timber and sailors
people.hiram.relations: This book calls him Huram. He sent cedars to David and now deals with Solomon.
people.hiram.meaning: Solomon asks him for timber and a skilled worker. Huram answers in writing and blesses the LORD. He sends Huram-abi, and wood by sea to Joppa. Later his sailors go with Solomon’s servants to Ophir for gold.
people.hiram-artisan.relations: Son of a woman of Dan and a man of Tyre (2:14). Kings words his mother’s family differently.
people.hiram-artisan.meaning: Huram the king sends him to Solomon. He makes the pillars, the sea, the pots, and other bronze vessels. He is not King Huram, though 4:11 calls him Huram.
people.araunah.role: Ornan, Jebusite owner of the threshing floor
people.araunah.relations: A Jebusite. The place David chose for the temple was his threshing floor.
people.araunah.meaning: This book calls him Ornan. Solomon builds the LORD’s house on his threshing floor on Mount Moriah. David had chosen that place. This book does not tell how David got it.
people.asaph-singer.role: Singer whose family leads temple music
people.asaph-singer.meaning: He stands with the singers when the ark enters the temple. Jahaziel, from his family, speaks before Jehoshaphat’s battle. Hezekiah’s Levites sing his words, and the book calls him a seer. His sons sing at Josiah’s Passover.
people.heman-singer.role: Singer whose sons serve in the temple
people.heman-singer.relations: He stands with Asaph and Jeduthun. His sons Jehuel and Shimei serve under Hezekiah.
people.heman-singer.meaning: He sings with cymbals and harps when the ark enters the temple. His sons help cleanse the temple for Hezekiah. Josiah’s singers follow his command.
people.jeduthun.relations: He stands with Asaph and Heman. His sons Shemaiah and Uzziel serve under Hezekiah.
people.jeduthun.meaning: He sings when the ark enters the temple. His sons help cleanse the temple for Hezekiah. In 35:15 the book calls him the king’s seer.
people.pharaoh-daughter-solomon.meaning: Solomon moves her out of David’s city to a house he built for her. He says the places the ark has come are holy. She says and does nothing in the account.
people.queen-sheba.role: Unnamed queen who tests Solomon with questions
people.queen-sheba.relations: She rules Sheba. She meets Solomon in Jerusalem.
people.queen-sheba.meaning: She comes with camels, spices, gold, and precious stones. Solomon answers all her hard questions. She says the report was true and blesses the LORD. They trade gifts, and she goes home.
people.nathan-prophet.role: Earlier prophet named in records and music orders
people.nathan-prophet.relations: Named with Ahijah and Iddo in 9:29. Named with David and Gad in 29:25.
people.nathan-prophet.meaning: He does not act in this book. His history is one record of Solomon’s reign. Hezekiah places the Levite players as David, Gad, and Nathan commanded.
people.ahijah-shiloh.role: Prophet whose word to Jeroboam comes true
people.ahijah-shiloh.relations: From Shiloh. He spoke the LORD’s word to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
people.ahijah-shiloh.meaning: He does not appear in person. His prophecy is one record of Solomon’s reign. When Rehoboam refuses the people, the book says the LORD’s word by Ahijah stands.
people.iddo-seer.role: Seer whose writings record three kings
people.iddo-seer.relations: The book names his writings for Solomon, Rehoboam, and Abijah.
people.iddo-seer.meaning: He does not act in the account. His visions about Jeroboam record Solomon’s acts. His other writings record Rehoboam and Abijah. Chapter 13 calls him a prophet.
people.jeroboam.role: First king of the northern tribes
people.jeroboam.meaning: He returns from Egypt and asks Rehoboam to lighten the people’s load. Israel leaves Rehoboam, and Jeroboam rules the north. He casts off the Levites and makes calf idols. Abijah defeats him, and the LORD strikes him dead.
people.rehoboam.relations: Son of Solomon and Naamah the Ammonitess. Father of Abijah.
people.rehoboam.meaning: He answers the people roughly, and most of Israel leaves him. Shemaiah stops him from fighting to win them back. He builds strong cities, then abandons the LORD’s law. Shishak takes the treasures, but Rehoboam humbles himself and is not destroyed.
people.adoram.relations: This book calls him Hadoram. Rehoboam sends him to the children of Israel.
people.adoram.meaning: He is over the men forced to work. Rehoboam sends him after Israel leaves. The people stone him to death, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem.
people.jesse.meaning: He does not act in this book. All Israel calls David “the son of Jesse” when they leave Rehoboam. Chapter 11 names him as the father of Eliab.
people.shemaiah.role: Man of God who speaks to Rehoboam twice
people.shemaiah.relations: He speaks to Rehoboam, Judah, and the princes. His histories record Rehoboam’s acts.
people.shemaiah.meaning: He tells Rehoboam’s army not to fight Israel, and the men go home. When Shishak attacks, he says Judah has left the LORD. The king and princes humble themselves. Shemaiah then says the LORD will not destroy them.
people.mahalath-rehoboam.meaning: Rehoboam takes her as a wife. She bears him Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. The book tells nothing more about her.
people.abihail-rehoboam.relations: Daughter of Eliab, the son of Jesse. Mother of Mahalath.
people.abihail-rehoboam.meaning: The book names her once, in Rehoboam’s family record. Her daughter Mahalath marries Rehoboam. Her father Eliab is a son of Jesse.
people.maacah-queen.relations: Granddaughter of Absalom and wife of Rehoboam. The text calls her mother of Abijah and of Asa.
people.maacah-queen.meaning: Rehoboam loves her above all his wives and makes her son Abijah chief. Later she makes an image for an Asherah. Asa removes her as queen mother. He cuts down the image and burns it at the brook Kidron.
people.abijam.role: King of Judah who defeats Jeroboam
people.abijam.relations: Son of Rehoboam. Chapter 11 names his mother Maacah, but 13:2 names Micaiah.
people.abijam.meaning: This book calls him Abijah. He stands on Mount Zemaraim and tells Israel not to fight the LORD. Jeroboam’s men trap Judah front and back. Judah cries to the LORD and wins, and Abijah takes Bethel.
people.shishak.relations: King of Egypt. He comes against Rehoboam in the king’s fifth year.
people.shishak.meaning: He takes Judah’s strong cities and comes to Jerusalem. He carries off the temple and palace treasures. He also takes Solomon’s gold shields. The LORD does not let him destroy Jerusalem.
people.naamah.relations: An Ammonitess. Named once, at the end of Rehoboam’s reign.
people.naamah.meaning: The book gives only her name and her people. She does nothing in the account.
people.aaron.role: Earlier priest whose sons serve at the altar
people.aaron.meaning: He does not act in this book. His sons are the priests who burn incense and offer sacrifices. Abijah says Jeroboam drove them out. Azariah tells Uzziah that only they may burn incense.
people.asa.role: King who trusts God, then turns to Syria
people.asa.relations: Son of Abijah. Father of Jehoshaphat.
people.asa.meaning: He removes foreign altars and calls on the LORD against Zerah’s army. After Azariah’s words, he leads Judah into a covenant. Later he pays Ben Hadad to attack Baasha. He jails the seer Hanani and seeks only doctors when sick.
people.zerah-cushite.role: Leader of the army Asa meets at Mareshah
people.zerah-cushite.relations: The reading translation calls him the Ethiopian. It names no family.
people.zerah-cushite.meaning: He comes to Mareshah with a million troops and three hundred chariots. Asa prays, and the LORD strikes Zerah’s army. Judah chases them to Gerar and takes much plunder.
people.azariah-oded.relations: Son of Oded. He is not King Uzziah or any priest named Azariah.
people.azariah-oded.meaning: The Spirit of God comes on him, and he goes to meet Asa. He says the LORD is with those who seek him. He tells Asa to be strong. Asa takes courage and renews the LORD’s altar.
people.oded-azariah.relations: Father of Azariah in 15:1. Verse 8 speaks of “the prophecy of Oded the prophet.”
people.oded-azariah.meaning: He does nothing in the account. Verse 8 gives the prophecy his name, not his son’s. The text does not explain the difference.
people.baasha.role: King of Israel who builds Ramah against Judah
people.baasha.meaning: He builds Ramah so no one can go in or out to Asa. Asa pays Ben Hadad to break his treaty with Baasha. Syria strikes Israel’s cities, and Baasha stops building. Asa carries away the stones and timber.
people.ben-hadad-asa.role: King of Syria paid to attack Israel
people.ben-hadad-asa.meaning: He lives at Damascus and has a treaty with Baasha. Asa sends him silver and gold from the temple. He sends his captains against Ijon, Dan, and Abel Maim. A later Ben Hadad fights Ahab in Kings.
people.hanani-seer.role: Seer who warns Asa about Syria
people.hanani-seer.relations: He speaks to Asa. Jehu the son of Hanani speaks to Jehoshaphat in chapter 19.
people.hanani-seer.meaning: He tells Asa he relied on Syria’s king and not on the LORD. He reminds Asa of the win over the Ethiopians. He says Asa will now have wars. Asa is angry and puts him in prison.
people.jehoshaphat.role: King who sends teachers, appoints judges, and prays
people.jehoshaphat.meaning: He sends princes, Levites, and priests to teach the law in Judah. He joins Ahab’s war, and Jehu the son of Hanani corrects him. He appoints judges and prays when three armies come. His ships with Ahaziah are wrecked.
people.amasiah.role: Captain who offers himself to the LORD
people.amasiah.relations: Son of Zichri. One of Jehoshaphat’s captains from Judah.
people.amasiah.meaning: He leads two hundred thousand mighty men. The book says he willingly offered himself to the LORD. It tells nothing more about him.
people.ahab.role: King of Israel who dies at Ramoth Gilead
people.ahab.relations: King of Israel and ally of Jehoshaphat. His daughter marries Jehoram of Judah.
people.ahab.meaning: He asks Jehoshaphat to fight for Ramoth Gilead. He jails Micaiah for saying he will fall. He goes into battle in disguise, but an arrow strikes him. He dies at sunset, and his house later leads Judah’s kings astray.
people.micaiah.role: Prophet who tells Ahab he will fall
people.micaiah.relations: Son of Imla. Ahab hates him and sends him to prison.
people.micaiah.meaning: A messenger asks him to agree with the other prophets. He says he will speak what God says. He tells of Israel scattered and a lying spirit in the prophets. Zedekiah strikes him, and Ahab jails him.
people.zedekiah-chenaanah.relations: Son of Chenaanah. One of Ahab’s prophets.
people.zedekiah-chenaanah.meaning: He makes iron horns and says Ahab will push the Syrians. He strikes Micaiah on the cheek. Micaiah says he will hide in an inner room. He is not the later king of Judah.
people.amon-governor.relations: Governor of the city. Named with Joash the king’s son.
people.amon-governor.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to him. He is to keep Micaiah in prison on bread and water. He is not Amon, the later king of Judah.
people.joash-prince.relations: Called the king’s son. Named with Amon the governor.
people.joash-prince.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken to him and to Amon. They are to hold Micaiah until Ahab returns. He is not Joash king of Judah or Joash king of Israel.
people.ahab-prophets.role: Four hundred prophets who promise Ahab victory
people.ahab-prophets.relations: Four hundred men gathered by Ahab. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah speaks among them.
people.ahab-prophets.meaning: Ahab asks them if he should go to Ramoth Gilead. They all say God will give it to the king. Micaiah says a lying spirit speaks through them. Ahab dies in the battle.
people.jehu-hanani.relations: Son of Hanani the seer. He is not Jehu the son of Nimshi.
people.jehu-hanani.meaning: He meets Jehoshaphat after the war with Ahab. He asks why the king helps the wicked. He also says good things are found in him. His history records Jehoshaphat’s acts.
people.amariah-chief.role: Chief priest over matters of the LORD
people.amariah-chief.meaning: Jehoshaphat sets him over the Jerusalem judges in all matters of the LORD. Zebadiah has the king’s matters. The book tells nothing more about him.
people.zebadiah-ishmael.role: Ruler over the king’s matters in court
people.zebadiah-ishmael.relations: Son of Ishmael and ruler of the house of Judah. Named with Amariah.
people.zebadiah-ishmael.meaning: Jehoshaphat sets him over the judges in all the king’s matters. Amariah has the matters of the LORD. The king tells them all to act with courage.
people.jahaziel.role: Levite who speaks before Jehoshaphat’s battle
people.jahaziel.meaning: The LORD’s Spirit comes on him in the assembly. He tells Judah not to fear, for the battle is God’s. He says where the enemy will be. Jehoshaphat bows down, and the army goes out singing.
people.azubah.meaning: The book names her once, at the end of Jehoshaphat’s reign. She does nothing in the account.
people.ahaziah-ahab.role: King of Israel who builds ships with Jehoshaphat
people.ahaziah-ahab.meaning: The book says he did very wickedly. Jehoshaphat joins him to build ships at Ezion Geber. The ships are wrecked. He is not Ahaziah king of Judah.
people.eliezer-dodavahu.role: Prophet who speaks against the ships
people.eliezer-dodavahu.relations: Son of Dodavahu, from Mareshah. He speaks against Jehoshaphat.
people.eliezer-dodavahu.meaning: He says the LORD has destroyed Jehoshaphat’s works for joining Ahaziah. The ships are wrecked and cannot go to Tarshish.
people.abraham.meaning: He does not act in this book. Jehoshaphat prays that God gave the land to Abraham’s offspring. He calls Abraham God’s friend. Hezekiah’s letters call the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
people.jehoram-judah.role: King of Judah who kills his brothers
people.jehoram-judah.relations: Son of Jehoshaphat. Husband of Ahab’s daughter. Father of Ahaziah.
people.jehoram-judah.meaning: He kills all his brothers with the sword. Edom and Libnah revolt from him. A letter from Elijah warns of plague and sickness. Raiders carry off his family, and he dies of a bowel disease.
people.elijah.relations: Called Elijah the prophet. His letter comes to Jehoram king of Judah.
people.elijah.meaning: His letter says Jehoram walked like Israel’s kings and killed his brothers. It warns of a plague on his people and family. It says Jehoram will have a bowel disease. Each thing then happens.
people.ahaziah-judah.role: King of Judah killed by Jehu
people.ahaziah-judah.relations: Youngest son of Jehoram and Athaliah, and father of Joash. Also called Jehoahaz (21:17) and Azariah (22:6).
people.ahaziah-judah.meaning: Jerusalem’s people make him king after raiders kill his older brothers. His mother counsels him to do evil. He visits the wounded Joram, and Jehu kills him. The text gives his age as forty-two, but 2 Kings 8:26 says twenty-two.
people.joram-israel.role: King of Israel wounded fighting Hazael
people.joram-israel.relations: Son of Ahab. The text calls him both Jehoram and Joram.
people.joram-israel.meaning: He fights Hazael at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wound him. He goes to Jezreel to heal. Ahaziah of Judah visits him there. He is not Jehoram king of Judah.
people.athaliah.relations: Mother of Ahaziah. The text calls her the daughter of Omri.
people.athaliah.meaning: She counsels her son Ahaziah to do evil. When he dies, she kills the royal children and reigns six years. Jehoiada crowns Joash, and she cries, “Treason!” The captains kill her at the horse gate.
people.omri.relations: Athaliah is called the daughter of Omri. Kings names him as Ahab’s father.
people.omri.meaning: He does not act in this book. The book names him once, in Ahaziah’s record.
people.hazael.role: King of Syria who fights Israel and Judah
people.hazael.relations: King of Syria. He fights Jehoram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah.
people.hazael.meaning: He fights at Ramoth Gilead against Jehoram and Ahaziah. His Syrians wound Jehoram. The book names him only in chapter 22.
people.jehu-nimshi.role: Man anointed to cut off Ahab’s house
people.jehu-nimshi.relations: Son of Nimshi and grandfather of Joash king of Israel. He is not Jehu the son of Hanani.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: The LORD anoints him to cut off Ahab’s house. He kills the princes of Judah who serve Ahaziah. His men find Ahaziah hiding in Samaria, and Ahaziah is killed.
people.jehosheba.relations: Daughter of King Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah, and wife of Jehoiada the priest.
people.jehosheba.meaning: This book calls her Jehoshabeath. She takes the child Joash from among the king’s sons being killed. She hides him and his nurse in a bedroom. He stays hidden in God’s house six years.
people.joash-nurse.relations: Nurse of Joash. Jehoshabeath hides her with the child.
people.joash-nurse.meaning: Jehoshabeath puts her and Joash in a bedroom. The book says nothing more about her.
people.joash-judah.role: Hidden child king who later kills Zechariah
people.joash-judah.meaning: He is hidden six years and crowned at age seven. He has a chest made and repairs the temple. After Jehoiada dies, he listens to the princes and serves idols. He has Zechariah stoned, and his own servants kill him.
people.jehoiada.role: Priest who crowns Joash and guides him
people.jehoiada.relations: Husband of Jehoshabeath and father of Zechariah. He raises and guides Joash.
people.jehoiada.meaning: He arms the captains and Levites and crowns Joash in the temple. He orders Athaliah killed outside the LORD’s house. He makes a covenant and helps repair the temple. He dies at 130 and is buried among the kings.
people.mattan-baal.role: Priest of Baal killed at his altars
people.mattan-baal.relations: Priest of Baal. The people kill him after Joash is crowned.
people.mattan-baal.meaning: The people break down the house of Baal after the covenant. They smash its altars and images. They kill Mattan before the altars.
people.zibiah.role: Mother of Joash king of Judah
people.zibiah.meaning: The book names her once, as the mother of Joash. She comes from Beersheba.
people.zechariah-jehoiada.relations: Son of Jehoiada the priest. Joash orders his death.
people.zechariah-jehoiada.meaning: The Spirit of God comes on him. He tells the people they left the LORD, so the LORD left them. They stone him in the temple court at the king’s command. Dying, he asks the LORD to see and repay.
people.zabad-shimeath.meaning: He and Jehozabad plot against Joash for the blood of Jehoiada’s sons. They kill the wounded king on his bed. Kings gives him a different name.
people.jehozabad.relations: Son of Shimrith the Moabitess (24:26). Kings spells his mother’s name differently.
people.jehozabad.meaning: He and Zabad plot against Joash after Zechariah’s death. They kill the wounded king on his bed. Amaziah later kills the servants who did it.
people.amaziah.role: King who defeats Edom and loses to Israel
people.amaziah.relations: Son of Joash and Jehoaddan. Father of Uzziah.
people.amaziah.meaning: He sends home the hired soldiers of Israel when a man of God warns him. He defeats Edom but brings back its gods. He challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth Shemesh. Plotters later kill him at Lachish.
people.jehoaddan.meaning: The book names her once, as Amaziah’s mother. She comes from Jerusalem.
people.joash-israel.role: King of Israel who defeats Amaziah
people.joash-israel.relations: Son of Jehoahaz and grandson of Jehu. He is not Joash king of Judah.
people.joash-israel.meaning: Amaziah dares him to meet face to face. He answers with a story of a thistle and a cedar. He defeats Judah at Beth Shemesh and captures Amaziah. He breaks Jerusalem’s wall and takes the temple gold to Samaria.
people.jehoahaz-israel.role: Father of Joash king of Israel
people.jehoahaz-israel.meaning: He does not act in this book. Chapter 25 names him as the father of Joash king of Israel. He is not Josiah’s son Jehoahaz in chapter 36.
people.amaziah-man-god.role: Unnamed man of God against the hired troops
people.amaziah-man-god.relations: He speaks to Amaziah before the fight with Edom.
people.amaziah-man-god.meaning: He tells Amaziah not to take Israel’s army, for the LORD is not with Israel. Amaziah asks about the hundred talents he paid. The man says the LORD can give much more. Amaziah sends the soldiers home.
people.amaziah-prophet.role: Unnamed prophet who questions Amaziah’s new gods
people.amaziah-prophet.relations: The LORD sends him to Amaziah after the win over Edom.
people.amaziah-prophet.meaning: He asks why Amaziah seeks gods that could not save their own people. The king tells him to stop or be struck down. He stops, but says God has decided to destroy Amaziah.
people.obed-edom-amaziah.role: Man named with the seized temple vessels
people.obed-edom-amaziah.relations: Named once, in 25:24, in Amaziah’s reign.
people.obed-edom-amaziah.meaning: The gold, silver, and vessels in God’s house are “with Obed-Edom.” Joash of Israel takes them all to Samaria. The text says nothing more about him.
people.azariah.role: Uzziah, king struck with leprosy over incense
people.azariah.meaning: He seeks God in the days of Zechariah, and God makes him prosper. He builds towers, digs cisterns, and arms a large army. When he is strong, he goes into the temple to burn incense. Leprosy breaks out on his forehead, and he lives apart until death.
people.jechiliah.meaning: The book names her once, as Uzziah’s mother. She comes from Jerusalem.
people.zechariah-uzziah.relations: The book says he had understanding in the vision of God.
people.zechariah-uzziah.meaning: Uzziah sets himself to seek God in Zechariah’s days. The book gives no words or acts of his. He is not Zechariah the son of Jehoiada.
people.azariah-uzziah-priest.role: Chief priest who stops Uzziah’s incense
people.azariah-uzziah-priest.relations: Chief priest. Eighty priests go in with him against the king.
people.azariah-uzziah-priest.meaning: He follows Uzziah into the temple with eighty priests. They tell the king that only Aaron’s sons may burn incense. They see leprosy on his forehead and thrust him out. He is not the chief priest Azariah of Hezekiah’s day.
people.jotham.role: King of Judah who builds and grows strong
people.jotham.meaning: He judges the people while his father Uzziah is a leper. As king he builds the temple’s upper gate, cities, and towers. He defeats Ammon and receives silver, wheat, and barley. He does right, but the people still act corruptly.
people.isaiah.meaning: He writes the acts of Uzziah. He prays with Hezekiah when Sennacherib’s men mock the LORD. The LORD then sends an angel against Assyria’s camp. His vision also records Hezekiah’s acts.
people.jerushah.relations: Daughter of Zadok. The text does not say this is David’s priest Zadok.
people.jerushah.meaning: The book names her once, as Jotham’s mother. She does nothing in the account.
people.ahaz.role: King of Judah who shuts the temple
people.ahaz.meaning: He makes images for the Baals and burns his children in the fire. Syria, Israel, Edom, and the Philistines defeat Judah. He pays Assyria’s king, who gives him trouble instead of help. He then shuts the temple doors and worships the gods of Damascus.
people.pekah.role: King of Israel who strikes Judah
people.pekah.relations: Son of Remaliah. He fights Ahaz of Judah.
people.pekah.meaning: He kills one hundred twenty thousand men of Judah in one day. Israel’s army then carries off two hundred thousand captives. The book says Judah had left the LORD.
people.pul.relations: King of Assyria. This book spells his name Tilgath-pilneser (28:20).
people.pul.meaning: Ahaz sends to Assyria for help against Edom and the Philistines. Tilgath-pilneser comes but gives him trouble. Ahaz gives him treasure from the temple and palace. It does not help.
people.oded-samaria.role: Prophet who tells Israel to free captives
people.oded-samaria.relations: A prophet of the LORD at Samaria. He is not Oded, Azariah’s father.
people.oded-samaria.meaning: He meets Israel’s army as it brings Judah’s captives to Samaria. He says they killed in a rage that reached heaven. He tells them to send the captives back. Four leaders agree, and the captives go home.
people.captive-care-leaders.role: Four leaders of Ephraim who free the captives
people.captive-care-leaders.meaning: They stand against the army and refuse the captives. They clothe the naked, feed them, and anoint them. They carry the weak on donkeys to Jericho. Then they return to Samaria.
people.hezekiah.role: King who reopens the temple and keeps Passover
people.hezekiah.relations: Son of Ahaz and Abijah. Father of Manasseh.
people.hezekiah.meaning: He opens the temple doors and has the Levites cleanse it. He invites Israel and Judah to Passover and prays for the unclean. He stops the springs and prays when Sennacherib comes. Later his heart is proud, but he humbles himself.
people.abi.meaning: This book calls her Abijah. It names her once, as Hezekiah’s mother. She is not King Abijah, Rehoboam’s son.
people.gad.role: Earlier seer named in Hezekiah’s music orders
people.gad.relations: Called the king’s seer. Named with David and Nathan the prophet.
people.gad.meaning: He does not act in this book. Hezekiah sets the Levites with cymbals and harps as David, Gad, and Nathan commanded. The book says the command came from the LORD by his prophets.
people.isaac.role: Earlier ancestor named in Hezekiah’s letters
people.isaac.meaning: He does not act in this book. Hezekiah’s letters call the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. The letters ask the northern tribes to turn back to that God.
people.azariah-hezekiah-priest.role: Chief priest who explains the heaps of offerings
people.azariah-hezekiah-priest.relations: Of the house of Zadok. Called ruler of God’s house under Hezekiah.
people.azariah-hezekiah-priest.meaning: Hezekiah asks about the heaps of offerings. Azariah says the priests have eaten enough and have plenty left. He and Hezekiah appoint men to oversee the stores. He is not the Azariah who opposed Uzziah.
people.conaniah-hezekiah.relations: A Levite. His brother Shimei is second to him.
people.conaniah-hezekiah.meaning: He rules over the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things brought to the temple. Ten overseers work under him and Shimei. Hezekiah and Azariah appoint them.
people.shimei-conaniah.relations: Brother of Conaniah the Levite. He serves under Hezekiah.
people.shimei-conaniah.meaning: He is second to Conaniah over the offerings and tithes. Ten overseers work under the two brothers. The book tells nothing more about him.
people.kore-imnah.role: Gatekeeper who gives out the free will offerings
people.kore-imnah.relations: Son of Imnah the Levite. Gatekeeper at the east gate.
people.kore-imnah.meaning: He is over the free will offerings of God. He gives out the LORD’s offerings and the most holy things. Six men under him give shares in the priests’ cities.
people.sennacherib.role: King of Assyria who threatens Jerusalem
people.sennacherib.relations: King of Assyria. His own children kill him in the house of his god.
people.sennacherib.meaning: He camps against Judah’s strong cities and attacks Lachish. His servants and letters say no god can save Jerusalem. An angel cuts down his mighty men, and he goes home in shame. His own royal record also tells of a war in Judah.
people.manasseh-king.role: King of Judah who humbles himself in Babylon
people.manasseh-king.meaning: He rebuilds the high places and sets an idol in God’s house. Assyria’s captains take him in chains to Babylon. He humbles himself and prays, and God brings him back. Then he removes the idols and builds up the LORD’s altar.
people.amon-king.role: King of Judah who does not humble himself
people.amon-king.meaning: He sacrifices to the images his father Manasseh made. He does not humble himself as Manasseh did. His servants kill him in his own house after two years. The people of the land make his son Josiah king.
people.josiah.meaning: He breaks down altars and images in Judah and beyond. He repairs the temple, hears the law book, and tears his clothes. He makes a covenant and keeps a great Passover. He ignores Neco’s warning and is shot at Megiddo.
people.hilkiah-priest.role: High priest who finds the book of the law
people.hilkiah-priest.relations: He works with Shaphan. He goes with the king’s men to Huldah.
people.hilkiah-priest.meaning: He finds the book of the LORD’s law while money is brought out. He gives it to Shaphan. He leads the king’s men to Huldah. At Passover he gives animals to the priests.
people.shaphan.role: Scribe who reads the book to Josiah
people.shaphan.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the temple. Hilkiah gives him the book of the law. He reports on the work and reads the book to the king. Then he goes with the others to Huldah.
people.huldah.role: Prophetess asked about the book of the law
people.huldah.relations: Wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe. She lives in Jerusalem’s second quarter.
people.huldah.meaning: Josiah’s men come to ask her about the book. She says the LORD will bring its curses on Jerusalem. She says Josiah will go to his grave in peace before that evil. The men carry her message to the king.
people.shallum-huldah.relations: Son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah. Husband of Huldah.
people.shallum-huldah.meaning: He is keeper of the wardrobe. The book names him only as Huldah’s husband.
people.ahikam.role: One of the men sent to Huldah
people.ahikam.meaning: Josiah commands him and four others to ask the LORD about the book. They go to Huldah the prophetess. They bring her message back to the king.
people.achbor.role: One of the men sent to Huldah
people.achbor.relations: This book calls him Abdon the son of Micah. Kings calls him Achbor the son of Micaiah.
people.achbor.meaning: Josiah sends him with Hilkiah, Ahikam, Shaphan, and Asaiah. They ask Huldah about the book of the law. He does nothing else in the book.
people.asaiah.relations: Called the king’s servant. He serves Josiah.
people.asaiah.meaning: Josiah sends him with four others after the book is read. They go to Huldah and bring back her message.
people.joah-joahaz.role: Recorder sent to repair the temple
people.joah-joahaz.relations: Son of Joahaz. Sent with Shaphan and Maaseiah by Josiah.
people.joah-joahaz.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the LORD’s house. The three men bring the gathered money to Hilkiah. He is not Joah the son of Asaph, Hezekiah’s recorder in Kings.
people.maaseiah-josiah.role: City governor sent to repair the temple
people.maaseiah-josiah.relations: Governor of the city. Sent with Shaphan and Joah by Josiah.
people.maaseiah-josiah.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the LORD’s house. The three men bring the gathered money to Hilkiah. The workmen use it to buy stone and timber.
people.necho.role: Egyptian king who warns Josiah, then controls Judah
people.necho.relations: King of Egypt. He removes Jehoahaz and makes Jehoiakim king.
people.necho.meaning: He marches to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. He tells Josiah that God sent him and to stay away. Josiah fights him at Megiddo and is shot. Neco later fines Judah and carries Joahaz to Egypt.
people.jeremiah.role: Prophet who laments Josiah and warns Zedekiah
people.jeremiah.relations: He laments Josiah. He speaks the LORD’s word to Zedekiah.
people.jeremiah.meaning: He laments when Josiah dies. Zedekiah does not humble himself before him. The book says the seventy empty years fulfill his word. Cyrus’s order also comes so that his word is done.
people.samuel.role: Earlier prophet named in a Passover comparison
people.samuel.meaning: He does not act in this book. The book says no Passover like Josiah’s was kept since Samuel’s days.
people.jehoahaz-judah.role: Josiah’s son removed by Egypt’s king
people.jehoahaz-judah.meaning: The people of the land make him king after Josiah. He reigns three months. Egypt’s king removes him and fines the land. Neco carries him to Egypt, and the text also spells his name Joahaz.
people.jehoiakim.role: King of Judah bound by Nebuchadnezzar
people.jehoiakim.meaning: Egypt’s king makes him king and changes his name from Eliakim. He does evil for eleven years. Nebuchadnezzar binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Some temple vessels go to Babylon too.
people.jehoiachin.role: King of Judah taken to Babylon
people.jehoiachin.meaning: He reigns three months and ten days and does evil. Nebuchadnezzar brings him to Babylon with the temple’s valuable vessels. This book says he was eight when he became king. Second Kings 24:8 says eighteen.
people.zedekiah.role: Last king of Judah before Jerusalem falls
people.zedekiah.relations: Kings calls him Josiah’s son and Jehoiachin’s uncle. This book calls him Jehoiachin’s brother (36:10).
people.zedekiah.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar makes him king and makes him swear by God. He does not humble himself before Jeremiah. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar. Then the Chaldeans burn the temple and carry the people away.
people.nebuchadnezzar.role: King of Babylon who destroys Jerusalem
people.nebuchadnezzar.relations: King of Babylon. He takes Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin and makes Zedekiah king.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: He binds Jehoiakim and takes temple vessels to Babylon. He brings Jehoiachin there and makes Zedekiah king. When Zedekiah rebels, his army burns the temple and breaks Jerusalem’s wall. He carries the people who are left to Babylon.
people.cyrus.role: King of Persia who lets the people go up
people.cyrus.relations: King of Persia. His order goes through all his kingdom in writing.
people.cyrus.meaning: In his first year the LORD stirs up his spirit. He says the LORD told him to build a house in Jerusalem. He tells any of the LORD’s people to go up. The book ends with his words.
places.gibeon.summary: God’s Tent of Meeting and Bezalel’s bronze altar stand at Gibeon. Solomon offers there, and God appears to him that night (chapter 1).
places.gibeon.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jerusalem.summary: Solomon builds the temple here, and Judah’s kings rule from the city. Kings repair or shut the temple in turn. The Chaldeans burn it in chapter 36.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location, not the temple site.
places.kiriath-jearim.summary: David had brought God’s ark up from Kiriath Jearim (1:4). He put it in a tent in Jerusalem.
places.kiriath-jearim.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.egypt.summary: Solomon buys horses and chariots from Egypt. Jeroboam flees there, and Shishak comes from there against Rehoboam. Neco later carries Joahaz to Egypt (chapter 36).
places.egypt.limits: The marker stands for a whole country, not one point.
places.tyre.summary: Huram rules Tyre. He sends Solomon timber and the craftsman Huram-abi (chapter 2).
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.lebanon.summary: Huram’s servants cut cedar, cypress, and algum trees in Lebanon for the temple (chapter 2). Solomon also builds there (8:6).
places.lebanon.limits: The marker stands for a broad mountain region, not one point.
places.joppa.summary: Huram’s men float the timber by sea to Joppa. Solomon’s men carry it up to Jerusalem (2:16).
places.joppa.limits: The marker shows the port’s general location.
places.jordan.summary: Solomon’s bronze vessels are cast in the plain of the Jordan (4:17). The place is between Succoth and Zeredah.
places.jordan.limits: The text gives no exact casting site. The marker shows the river area only.
places.sinai.summary: Chapter 5 calls the place Horeb. Moses put the two tablets in the ark there. The LORD made a covenant with Israel there (5:10).
places.sinai.limits: Scholars dispute which mountain this is. The marker is not a proven site.
places.hamath.summary: People come to Solomon’s feast from as far as the entrance of Hamath (7:8). Solomon builds storage cities in Hamath (8:4).
places.hamath.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The “entrance of Hamath” is not a fixed point.
places.beth-horon.summary: Solomon builds upper and lower Beth Horon as walled cities (8:5). Israel’s sent-back soldiers raid Judah’s cities as far as Beth Horon (25:13).
places.beth-horon.limits: One marker stands for both towns.
places.ezion-geber.summary: Solomon goes to Ezion Geber and Eloth on the seashore in Edom (8:17). Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah build ships there, and the ships are wrecked (chapter 20). Uzziah rebuilds Eloth (26:2).
places.ezion-geber.limits: Scholars dispute the exact site near the Gulf of Aqaba. The marker shows the general area.
places.edom.summary: Edom revolts against Jehoram and makes its own king (chapter 21). Amaziah later defeats its men and brings home its gods (chapter 25).
places.edom.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.
places.sheba.summary: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon and comes to test him. Then she returns to her own land (chapter 9).
places.sheba.limits: The marker stands for a broad southern Arabian region. It is not her proven capital.
places.shechem.summary: All Israel comes to Shechem to make Rehoboam king. He answers them roughly there, and the kingdom splits (chapter 10).
places.shechem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.bethlehem.summary: Rehoboam builds Bethlehem as one of Judah’s cities for defense (11:6).
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.tekoa.summary: Rehoboam builds Tekoa for defense (11:6). Jehoshaphat’s army goes out into the wilderness of Tekoa, singing (20:20).
places.tekoa.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. The wilderness around it has no exact edge.
places.adullam.summary: Rehoboam builds Adullam as one of Judah’s cities for defense (11:7).
places.adullam.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.gath.summary: Rehoboam builds Gath as a city for defense (11:8). Uzziah later breaks down its wall (26:6).
places.gath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.lachish.summary: Rehoboam builds Lachish for defense (11:9). Amaziah flees there and is killed (25:27). Sennacherib attacks it while his servants go to Jerusalem (32:9).
places.lachish.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.hebron.summary: Rehoboam builds Hebron as one of Judah’s walled cities (11:10).
places.hebron.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.bethel.summary: Abijah chases Jeroboam and takes Bethel with its villages (13:19).
places.bethel.limits: The site is a proposed one. The marker shows its general location.
places.mareshah.summary: Rehoboam builds Mareshah for defense (11:8). Asa meets Zerah’s army there (chapter 14). Eliezer, who warns Jehoshaphat, comes from this town (20:37).
places.mareshah.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. The valley of Zephathah is not marked.
places.gerar.summary: Asa’s army chases Zerah’s men to Gerar. Judah strikes the cities around it and takes much plunder (14:13–14).
places.gerar.limits: Tell Haror is a proposed site. The marker is close, not exact.
places.kidron.summary: Asa burns Maacah’s image at the brook Kidron (15:16). Hezekiah’s Levites carry temple filth there (chapter 29). The people throw altars into it (chapter 30).
places.kidron.limits: The marker shows the valley east of Jerusalem, not an exact spot.
places.damascus.summary: Ben Hadad lives at Damascus when Asa pays him (16:2). Syria sends Judah’s plunder and captives there (chapters 24, 28). Ahaz sacrifices to its gods (28:23).
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ramah.summary: Baasha builds Ramah to shut Asa in. When he stops, Asa carries off its stones and timber (chapter 16).
places.ramah.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location in Benjamin.
places.dan.summary: Ben Hadad’s captains strike Dan (16:4). Hezekiah’s Passover call goes from Beersheba to Dan (30:5).
places.dan.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.mizpah.summary: Asa builds Geba and Mizpah with the stones and timber from Ramah (16:6).
places.mizpah.limits: Scholars are not sure which site in Benjamin is Mizpah. The marker is a proposal.
places.samaria.summary: Ahab hosts Jehoshaphat at Samaria, and Micaiah speaks at its gate (chapter 18). Ahaziah hides there (22:9). Oded meets Israel’s army there, and the captives go free (chapter 28).
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ramoth-gilead.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat fight Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and Ahab dies (chapter 18). The Syrians wound Joram there (22:5).
places.ramoth-gilead.limits: Scholars dispute the site. The marker shows one general area.
places.beersheba.summary: Jehoshaphat goes among the people from Beersheba to Ephraim’s hills (19:4). Zibiah, mother of Joash, comes from Beersheba (24:1). Hezekiah’s Passover call starts there (30:5).
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.en-gedi.summary: Messengers tell Jehoshaphat that a great army is at Hazazon Tamar. The text says that is En Gedi (20:2).
places.en-gedi.limits: The marker shows the general location, not the army’s camp.
places.moab.summary: The children of Moab come with Ammon against Jehoshaphat. The armies then destroy each other (chapter 20).
places.moab.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.
places.libnah.summary: Libnah revolts against Jehoram when Edom does. The book says he had left the LORD (21:10).
places.libnah.limits: Scholars dispute where Libnah was. The marker is a proposal.
places.jezreel.summary: The wounded Joram goes to Jezreel to heal. Ahaziah of Judah visits him there (22:6).
places.jezreel.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.beth-shemesh.summary: Joash of Israel defeats and captures Amaziah at Beth Shemesh (chapter 25). The Philistines take the town in the days of Ahaz (28:18).
places.beth-shemesh.limits: Ain Shems is a proposed site. The marker shows the town, not the battle spot.
places.ashdod.summary: Uzziah breaks down the wall of Ashdod. He builds cities in its country (26:6).
places.ashdod.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jericho.summary: Four leaders of Ephraim bring Judah’s freed captives to Jericho, to their brothers. The text calls it the city of palm trees (28:15).
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.assyria.summary: Ahaz sends to Assyria’s kings for help and gets trouble (chapter 28). Sennacherib comes from Assyria against Judah (chapter 32). Its captains take Manasseh away (33:11).
places.assyria.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.
places.babylon.summary: Princes of Babylon send men to Hezekiah (32:31). Manasseh is carried there and returns (chapter 33). Nebuchadnezzar takes kings, vessels, and people there (chapter 36).
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.megiddo.summary: Josiah fights Neco in the valley of Megiddo. Archers shoot him there (35:22–23).
places.megiddo.limits: The marker shows the town, not the battle spot in the valley.
places.carchemish.summary: Neco goes up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. Josiah goes out against him on the way (35:20).
places.carchemish.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
sources.web.limits: The text alone cannot prove its numbers, dates, or what people looked like. It cannot prove private motives.
sources.atlas-exodus.limits: The route shown is a study tradition. It does not prove a sea crossing or a Sinai site.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the map labels for the setting. The linked atlas also includes LDS commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Marker positions are estimates. A town marker does not prove that an event happened there.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain helps show the land. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.tuell-chronicles.summary: Tuell describes family lists as memory and David’s temple role. He also covers debates about how the books were written.
sources.tuell-chronicles.limits: This is opening background only. The full book list and the commentaries it cites were not available. Scholars still dispute who wrote Chronicles and when.
sources.mcclellan-chronicles.summary: McClellan proposes that Chronicles reflects a contest over priestly authority. He warns against reading modern categories into the past.
sources.mcclellan-chronicles.limits: This is one reading, not proof of every author’s motive. A machine made the transcript, so it may contain errors. The audio was not checked. Other interview topics are not used here.
sources.japhet-record.limits: The full commentary was not read. The record confirms the work, not its arguments.
sources.cfm-chronicles-context.summary: The article explains that the history books select what they tell. It compares Chronicles with Samuel and Kings.
sources.millard-hezekiah.limits: This is one scholar’s argument, not an agreed verdict. Weigh royal boasting and the Bible’s religious claims separately. The article does not prove the Bible’s death total on its own.
sources.taylor-prism.limits: The catalog is a primary object record. The direct museum page failed to open. Its full inscription was not read there. Royal totals are claims, not checked counts.
sources.luther-2-chronicles.limits: This is a scholar’s teaching overview. Its views on author, date, and literary form do not prove each event.
sources.schaser-2-chronicles.limits: These are named scholars’ readings, not conclusions all scholars share. Links to later Christian texts are comparisons made by the interpreter.
sources.wiki-2-chronicles.summary: The opening gives the book’s structure and points to other works to read.
sources.wiki-2-chronicles.limits: Use this source for background only. Its claims about author, writing date, and order of events are not taken as certain. They are checked against scholarship.
sources.cfm-2026-30.limits: This is faith teaching and application. The lesson does not prove ancient battles or what a disease was.
sources.lds-2-chronicles.limits: This is LDS teaching, not a finding from digs. A named place link does not prove every building detail.
sources.met-244562.limits: Its form differs from the temple stands described in Kings. It is a comparison, not a model of those stands.
chapters.*.mapNote: Points mark named towns and broad regions in the book. Many ancient sites are only roughly placed.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The map draws no route for this book.
sources.cfm-chronicles-context.limits: This source gives book context. It is not a dedicated 1 Chronicles weekly lesson. Faith applications and historical comparison remain distinct.
